snapshot.scope: github-runner/** (19 untracked files) plus root README.md diff vs HEAD

findings.issue: `prepare` refuses every official Linux/macOS runner archive (in-tree relative symlinks under externals/node*/bin)
findings.behavioral_description: Following setup.md with the real release asset ends in 'Archive links and special entries require manual review', exit 1; the receipted preparation path, inspect readback and resume guarantees are unreachable on real input, so agents fall back to bare tar with none of the guards.
findings.acceptance_check: In a mktemp dir outside the project, as a non-root user: python3 scripts/prepare_runner.py prepare --archive actions-runner-osx-arm64-2.338.0.tar.gz --sha256 df4cebda25c86a886ed204e49fee63f5c2e7cec5f447b5c98440a826bbdf9df2 --version 2.338.0 --directory <resolved-parent>/instance --expected-user "$(id -un)" currently exits 1; passes when it exits 0, .preparation.json reads status prepared, and readlink instance/externals/node20/bin/npm prints ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js.

findings.issue: `inspect` rejects real .runner files because the runner writes them with a UTF-8 BOM
findings.behavioral_description: The only sanctioned credential-safe readback of registration identity fails on every real instance with 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM', pushing the agent to read .runner by hand next to .credentials.
findings.acceptance_check: printf '\xef\xbb\xbf{"agentId":42,"agentName":"box","gitHubUrl":"https://github.com/acme/widget"}' > <tmp>/bomcase/.runner && python3 scripts/prepare_runner.py inspect --directory <tmp>/bomcase currently exits 1; passes when it exits 0 and prints "agentId": 42. On a real host: head -c 3 .runner | xxd shows efbb bf and the same inspect succeeds.

findings.issue: Every hosted fallback of the selector is silent and reason-free; misconfiguration, expired PAT and 'runner busy' are byte-identical
findings.behavioral_description: A misspelled variable, a RUNNER_LABELS array missing the architecture, an expired token, a stale TRUSTED_RUNNER_REF, an API error and a busy runner all produce exactly runner="ubuntu-24.04", exit 0, nothing on stderr; CI stays green on hosted runners indefinitely and the persistent host is silently never used; a local dry run dies on 'Invalid selector output path' without naming GITHUB_OUTPUT.
findings.acceptance_check: env -i HOSTED_RUNNER=ubuntu-24.04 GITHUB_OUTPUT=/dev/null GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widget PREFERRED_RUNNER_NAME=build-box PREFERRED_RUNNER_LABEL=widget-ci RUNNER_LABELS='Linux,X64' RUNNER_READ_TOKEN=x TRUSTED_EVENT=true python3 github-runner/scripts/select_runner.py currently prints exactly runner="ubuntu-24.04" with empty stderr; passes when a line naming the non-secret reason (e.g. reason=RUNNER_LABELS-not-json-array) is emitted. Corroborating: select() with RUNNER_LABELS='["Linux"]' and select() with a busy runner must return distinguishable results.

findings.issue: Trusted-ref gate github.ref == vars.TRUSTED_RUNNER_REF is case-insensitive; a case-variant unprotected branch is routed to the persistent host
findings.behavioral_description: A write collaborator who cannot push to the protected trusted branch pushes refs/heads/MAIN; the expression evaluates true, TRUSTED_EVENT is set, and the checks job checks out the attacker's commit on the self-hosted host.
findings.acceptance_check: In a mktemp copy with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1: GITHUB_OUTPUT=/dev/null HOSTED_RUNNER=ubuntu-24.04 TRUSTED_EVENT=true GITHUB_REF=refs/heads/MAIN TRUSTED_RUNNER_REF=refs/heads/main GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widget RUNNER_READ_TOKEN=x PREFERRED_RUNNER_NAME=w PREFERRED_RUNNER_LABEL=repo-ci RUNNER_LABELS='["Linux","X64"]' python3 scripts/select_runner.py must print runner="ubuntu-24.04" before any API request; today the selector ignores GITHUB_REF and with a stubbed API would emit the self-hosted label array. After the fix test_select_runner.py carries a case-variant subtest.

findings.issue: HOSTED_RUNNER rejection names neither the received value nor the accepted subset, which exists only in source
findings.behavioral_description: An operator who picks ubuntu-22.04-arm from GitHub's own standard-runner table sees 'HOSTED_RUNNER is required and must be an approved standard GitHub-hosted label' on the first run; the primary journey stops and resolves only by reading source.
findings.acceptance_check: env -i HOSTED_RUNNER=ubuntu-22.04-arm GITHUB_OUTPUT=/dev/null python3 github-runner/scripts/select_runner.py currently fails without naming the received value or any accepted label; passes when stderr names the received value and enumerates the accepted labels.

findings.issue: RUNNER_LABELS must contain one OS and one architecture label; the docs never say so and the failure is a silent fallback
findings.behavioral_description: An operator copies the labels shown on the runner page (self-hosted, Linux) or sets just the OS; every push runs on hosted Ubuntu with zero API calls and nothing in the docs points at RUNNER_LABELS as the cause.
findings.acceptance_check: grep -n 'RUNNER_LABELS' github-runner/references/ci.md fails today (the row mentions neither an architecture-label requirement nor the silent fallback); passes once the row states one OS label and one architecture label are required, extras are AND-matched, and any other array returns HOSTED_RUNNER before any API request; select(env | RUNNER_LABELS='["Linux"]', fetch) must still return the fallback with zero fetch calls.

findings.issue: Workflow concurrency group (workflow + ref, cancel-in-progress) cancels the documented preferred/force_hosted acceptance pair
findings.behavioral_description: Pushing the candidate and then dispatching the preferred and force_hosted runs on the same ref, as ci.md instructs, places all runs in one cancel-in-progress group; the required preferred-host evidence ends as cancelled and an agent may misreport it as a routing failure.
findings.acceptance_check: On a throwaway repo: gh workflow run "Preferred runner CI" --ref <candidate>; gh workflow run "Preferred runner CI" --ref <candidate> -f force_hosted=true; sleep 60; gh run list --workflow "Preferred runner CI" --branch <candidate> --json conclusion,event shows a cancelled conclusion today and none once fixed.

findings.issue: The digest the documented gh api command returns is sha256:<hex> and prepare --sha256 rejects it
findings.behavioral_description: The documented command yields digest sha256:<hex>; passing it verbatim fails with 'Invalid digest or version', which names neither the argument nor the prefix, nudging the operator to recompute the digest, which the doc forbids.
findings.acceptance_check: prepare --sha256 sha256:<official hex> currently exits 1 with 'Invalid digest or version'; passes when it is accepted (or the doc shows the exact stripping command) and the message splits --sha256 from --version and echoes the offending value.

findings.issue: status: incomplete after an interrupted extraction has no documented or coded forward path
findings.behavioral_description: After a dropped SSH session mid-extraction, inspect reports incomplete, re-running prepare is refused, the doc forbids cleanup or overwrite and names no resume; the fresh-install journey stalls at step 2.
findings.acceptance_check: After the SIGKILL fixture (patch shutil.copyfileobj to os._exit(137) on the 50th call, run prepare), a documented recovery sequence ends with inspect printing "status": "prepared"; today no documented sequence does.

findings.issue: Refusal messages of prepare/inspect/renderer name the wrong condition: macOS /tmp, /var, mktemp -d paths refused as 'symlinks' without the resolved path; expected-user mismatch reported as 'not root'
findings.behavioral_description: On macOS a directory the operator created one second ago is refused as having symlink path components with no resolved path offered, and a missing or relative directory gets the same message; a mistyped --expected-user is reported as a root problem naming neither account.
findings.acceptance_check: python3 scripts/prepare_runner.py inspect --directory /tmp/x on macOS currently prints 'Use an absolute resolved directory without symlinks'; passes when the message shows /tmp/x resolves to /private/tmp/x and says to pass that; prepare --expected-user ci_user as user diego currently says 'not root'; passes when it names the current and expected accounts.

findings.issue: Helper CLI contract (preconditions, inspect JSON shape, receipt states, runner= line, exit codes) is neither consistent across helpers nor documented in docs or --help
findings.behavioral_description: An agent using the docs as its spec cannot learn the inspect output shape, the receipt states, or whether an exit code means 'fix your command' or 'guard refused' (1/2 differ per helper); ten of thirteen flags have no help text.
findings.acceptance_check: python3 scripts/macos_service.py --help currently shows six bare flag names; passes when every flag has a help string stating meaning and precondition, and a helper reference documents per helper the preconditions, outputs, JSON keys, receipt states and one exit-code contract (2 usage, 1 guard refusal, 0 done).

findings.issue: Selector queries by name only and cannot enforce the label-uniqueness / hosted-label-collision invariant the routing depends on
findings.behavioral_description: When a second runner later carries the custom label, or a self-hosted box is labelled ubuntu-latest, the selector still finds exactly one runner named as configured and emits the label set; trusted-ref jobs and the PAT-bearing select job can land on an unvetted host.
findings.acceptance_check: With a fixture inventory containing two runners labelled repo-ci, select() currently returns the label list; passes when it returns the hosted fallback (with reason) and when a self-hosted runner carrying HOSTED_RUNNER or ubuntu-latest also triggers the fallback.

findings.issue: On Windows prepare silently drops the parent-ownership and not-root guards the docs promise on every platform
findings.behavioral_description: An elevated Windows shell whose username matches --expected-user can extract into a parent owned by another account; both guards are hasattr-gated no-ops while the docs promise the same guards everywhere.
findings.acceptance_check: On Windows, prepare from an elevated shell currently succeeds; passes when it refuses or emits an explicit platform-unsupported message that is also stated in setup.md.

findings.issue: Six safety guards are non-pinning in the test suite (three pagination guards masked by except Exception, 64 KiB cap, root and parent-owner guards without a seam)
findings.behavioral_description: Deleting any of six documented safety guards leaves the 24 tests green; the pagination and size invariants the docs cite can regress silently.
findings.acceptance_check: Deleting 'or len(batch) < 100' from select_runner.py currently leaves the suite green; passes when at least one test fails for each of the six mutations.

findings.issue: Service PATH story contradicts the runner: config.sh writes .path and runsvc.sh exports it, overriding the plist --path and the ci.md claim
findings.behavioral_description: After any normal registration the daemon runs with whatever PATH the runtime account had in the shell that ran config.sh, not the rendered one; an operator who adds --path sees no effect and ci.md states the opposite of the runner's behaviour.
findings.acceptance_check: The rendered service-plan.txt and platforms.md currently never mention .path/.env; passes when both state the precedence and the plan tells the operator to inspect/set .path as the runtime account.

findings.issue: Linux guidance has root run sudo ./svc.sh from the runtime-account-owned runner tree (runtime-writable code executed as root), unlike the macOS branch
findings.behavioral_description: Any code that ran as the runtime account can rewrite svc.sh, the .service file or the templates, and the next sudo ./svc.sh executes it as root.
findings.acceptance_check: platforms.md Linux section currently shows sudo ./svc.sh as the primary procedure; passes when it installs once, before any job has run, from an administrator-owned reviewed copy (or a rendered systemd unit) and manages the unit only via systemctl, with an explicit never-re-run rule.

findings.issue: The rendered macOS plan bakes the local staging path into the privileged sudo install line; off-target rendering requires hand-editing a sudo command
findings.behavioral_description: When the plan is rendered on the workstation because Python may be absent on the target, the plutil -lint and sudo install lines fail on the target with 'No such file' and the operator must edit a privileged line by hand.
findings.acceptance_check: Rendering with --output-dir <workstation path> currently embeds that path in the sudo install line; passes when a --target-staging-dir or an explicit STAGED_PLIST= placeholder line is used by both commands.

findings.issue: The default-branch bootstrap gate is invisible: buried mid-paragraph in ci.md and surfaced in the run only as Python's 'can't open file'
findings.behavioral_description: The operator adds the helper and workflow on a feature branch and pushes; the sparse checkout succeeds with nothing and the run dies with a Python file-not-found error that never names RUNNER_SELECTOR_SHA or the bootstrap rule, which is sentence 7 of a 188-word paragraph.
findings.acceptance_check: ci.md 'Prepare the selector' currently has no heading for the bootstrap gate; passes when it is numbered steps with a 'Bootstrap on the default branch first' subsection and ci.yml has a guard step before route that fails with an ::error:: naming the rule.

findings.issue: Archive refusal messages ('links and special entries', 'missing entry points', 'checksum mismatch') name no entry, expected name or computed value
findings.behavioral_description: The operator must re-list the archive by hand to find which member, which required name, or what digest was computed.
findings.acceptance_check: prepare on an archive with a symlink member currently prints the generic message; passes when it names the first offending member and type, the missing required names, and the computed digest beside the expected one.

findings.issue: macOS renderer rejects legitimate account names (uppercase, dots) and never names the offending argument
findings.behavioral_description: An account created as Build or build.ci is rejected with 'Choose a dedicated standard runtime account.', which reads as a policy objection; messages never say which flag failed, so operators rename working accounts or guess.
findings.acceptance_check: macos_service.py --account Build ... currently prints 'Choose a dedicated standard runtime account.'; passes when it either accepts [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63} or says 'lowercase letters only' with the flag name and value, with 'reserved account' as a separate message.

findings.issue: README Checks cites a quick_validate.py that is not in the repo, not linked, and fails on an undeclared PyYAML dependency; no actionlint install pointer
findings.behavioral_description: A contributor following Checks top to bottom cannot run the first instruction; the documented py_compile/unittest lines also litter __pycache__ into the skill folder when run without -B.
findings.acceptance_check: A fresh clone's Checks section currently has an instruction that cannot be executed from docs and terminal; passes when it links the validator's source and states its PyYAML requirement (or replaces it with an in-repo dependency-free check), adds an actionlint install pointer, and uses python3 -B or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.

findings.issue: Skill README install/invocation form (--skill, 'after published', $github-runner) diverges from the root README and sibling convention (@<skill>, -g)
findings.behavioral_description: A reader coming from the root table gets two contracts for one action and may run the @github-runner form before merge and get a not-found while the skill README hedges and the root README does not.

findings.issue: actions/checkout@v6 is a mutable tag in both jobs of a template that cites the hardening guide and SHA-pins its own selector
findings.behavioral_description: Both jobs, including the PAT-bearing selector job, resolve a moving tag at run time while the template's stated posture is full-SHA pinning.

findings.issue: .preparation.json carries no format/version stamp and inspect has no version check
findings.behavioral_description: A later helper release that adds or renames receipt fields leaves older receipts reporting nulls with no indication of age, and an older helper silently drops newer fields.

findings.issue: The runtime account is --expected-user / --account / $RUNNER_ACCOUNT; 'label' means three different things across surfaces
findings.behavioral_description: An operator passes the routing label to the renderer's --label and gets a LaunchDaemon named after it; the same concept is named differently in every helper and document.

findings.issue: remote_command.py rejects admin@host without pointing at --admin-account and host:2222 as 'not a valid IP address'
findings.behavioral_description: The two most common SSH habits are rejected with messages that do not say what to do instead; the colon routes a hostname to the IPv6 branch.

findings.issue: Same facts restated in up to eight places (dedicated-account rule, Python floor, test command, label verification date)
findings.behavioral_description: All copies agree today; the first edit to one copy makes the others wrong, and the agent-facing copies drift on a different reflex than the human README.

findings.issue: tests/scenarios.md mixes the reusable scenario spec with a dated evaluation log whose absolute counts will drift
findings.behavioral_description: Absolute repository-wide test counts and process history ship to every installer and will be wrong after the next test is added anywhere in the repo.

findings.issue: platforms.md bundles common rules + three OS branches + availability while SKILL.md tells the agent to load one branch
findings.behavioral_description: An agent on a Linux host carries the macOS and Windows material in context for the whole session.

findings.issue: No diagram anywhere; the four-gate lifecycle, selector routing, credential boundaries and macOS daemon conversion are prose only
findings.behavioral_description: Decision-tree questions such as which condition sent a job to hosted, or LaunchAgent versus LaunchDaemon, require a full prose read.
